# core/tls13client.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/tls13client.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

A TLS 1.3 client that does no input or output of
its own. The caller reads bytes from a connection and passes them to
`tls13c_feed`; whatever the client wants to send is appended to a buffer
the caller writes to the connection, and the data received from the peer is
appended to another. So the same code runs over a socket, a pipe or a test.

It speaks three suites, TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 and
TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256, with X25519, and checks
the server: the certificate chain against the trusted roots the caller
gives (X.509 with RSA, ECDSA (P-256 and P-384) and Ed25519 signatures made
with SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512, validity, host name, CA flags and key
usage), the CertificateVerify signature (ed25519, ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256,
ecdsa_secp384r1_sha384, rsa_pss_rsae_sha256 or rsa_pss_rsae_sha384) and
the Finished message. It sends no client
certificate, offers no resumption or early data, and accepts a KeyUpdate
and NewSessionTicket messages.

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, and the keys and
secrets the state holds always have the lengths the record layer needs.
Not proved: that the protocol is followed; the tests run a handshake with
an OpenSSL server (tests/tls.sh) and feed damaged and truncated flights.
Not done: certificate path length and name constraints, extended key usage
and revocation checks; session tickets; a
check that the random values are random (the caller supplies them).

`import "core/tls13client.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/sha256.bastio](core-sha256.md), [core/sha512.bastio](core-sha512.md), [core/hkdf.bastio](core-hkdf.md), [core/tls13.bastio](core-tls13.md), [core/der.bastio](core-der.md), [core/p256.bastio](core-p256.md), [core/rsa.bastio](core-rsa.md), [core/tls13hs.bastio](core-tls13hs.md), [core/aes.bastio](core-aes.md), [core/aesgcm.bastio](core-aesgcm.md), [core/chacha20.bastio](core-chacha20.md), [core/poly1305.bastio](core-poly1305.md), [core/chacha20poly1305.bastio](core-chacha20poly1305.md), [core/tls13record.bastio](core-tls13record.md), [core/x25519.bastio](core-x25519.md), [core/ed25519.bastio](core-ed25519.md), [core/p384.bastio](core-p384.md), [core/x509.bastio](core-x509.md).

## Types and constants

### `Tls13Client`

```bastio
struct Tls13Client {
  state: u64, priv_key: Bytes, name: Bytes, transcript: Bytes,
  hs_secret: Bytes, c_hs: Bytes, s_hs: Bytes,
  suite: u64, c_suite: u64, s_suite: u64,
  c_key: Bytes, c_iv: Bytes, s_key: Bytes, s_iv: Bytes,
  c_secret: Bytes, s_secret: Bytes, c_seq: u64, s_seq: u64,
  inbuf: Bytes, hsbuf: Bytes, leaf: Bytes,
  verify: bool, verdict: u64, alpn: Bytes, sent_close: bool,
  allow12: bool, only12: bool, v12: bool, step: u64, rnd: Bytes, ms: Bytes, ems: bool, cs12: u64,
  sk_kind: u64, sk_a: Bytes, sk_b: Bytes,
  creq: u64, croots: Bytes, cleaf: Bytes, cnow: u64, cverdict: u64,
  ck_kind: u64, ck_nonce: Bytes
}
```

The state of one connection. `state` is 0 waiting for the ServerHello, 1
for EncryptedExtensions, 2 for the Certificate, 3 for CertificateVerify, 4
for the server's Finished, 5 connected, 6 closed by the peer, 7 failed.
`verify` is false when a chain the roots do not vouch for is accepted
anyway (`verdict` then says why it would have been refused); `alpn` holds
the protocols offered, then the one the server chose. `sent_close` is true
once `tls13c_shutdown` has said goodbye: nothing more is sent, but what the
server still sends is read. `allow12` offers TLS 1.2 too; `v12` is true
once the server chose it (cipher suite `cs12`); `step` is then where the
TLS 1.2 handshake is (0 Certificate, 1 ServerKeyExchange, 2
ServerHelloDone, 3 the server's ChangeCipherSpec, 4 its Finished), `rnd`
the client and then the server random, `ms` the premaster and then the
master secret, `ems` whether it is an extended master secret. The
server of core/tls13server keeps its signing key in `sk_kind` (0 none, 1
RSA with the modulus in `sk_a` and the private exponent in `sk_b`, 2
ECDSA P-256 with the scalar in `sk_a`).

## Functions

### `tls13c_new`

```bastio
fn tls13c_new(random: &Bytes, session_id: &Bytes, priv_key: &Bytes, name: &Bytes, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> Tls13Client
  requires blen(random) == 32 && blen(session_id) == 32 && blen(priv_key) == 32 && blen(name) <= 255
  ensures tls13c_ok(result) && result.state == 0
  ensures vlen(out) > vlen(old(out))
```

Starts a connection to the server named `name` (at most 255 bytes): the
ClientHello, as a record, is appended to `out`. `random`, `session_id`
and `priv_key` are 32 bytes each and must be unpredictable and not used
again; the private key stays in the client.

Example:

```bastio
let r = balloc(32);
let s = balloc(32);
let k = balloc(32);
let name = bfrom("example.com");
let mut out = text_new();
let c = tls13c_new(r, s, k, name, &mut out);
let first = vec_get(out, 0);
let st = tls13c_state(c);
tls13c_free(c);
vec_free(out);
bfree(name);
bfree(k);
bfree(s);
bfree(r);
if first != 22 || st != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13c_new_with`

```bastio
fn tls13c_new_with(random: &Bytes, session_id: &Bytes, priv_key: &Bytes, name: &Bytes, alpn: &Bytes, verify: bool, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> Tls13Client
  requires blen(random) == 32 && blen(session_id) == 32 && blen(priv_key) == 32 && blen(name) <= 255 && blen(alpn) <= 256
  ensures tls13c_ok(result) && result.state == 0
  ensures vlen(out) > vlen(old(out))
```

`tls13c_new` that also offers the application protocols `alpn` (RFC
7301; the ProtocolNameList without its length, each name behind a one-byte
length, at most 256 bytes, empty for none; `tls13c_alpn` tells which one
the server chose). With `verify` false a certificate chain that the roots
do not vouch for, or that is for another name, is accepted (the server
must still prove it holds the key of its certificate); `tls13c_verdict`
then says what was wrong with it.

Example:

```bastio
let r = balloc(32);
let s = balloc(32);
let k = balloc(32);
let name = bfrom("example.com");
let mut a = text_new();
text_push(&mut a, 2);
text_push_str(&mut a, "h2");
let alpn = text_finish(a);
let mut out = text_new();
let c = tls13c_new_with(r, s, k, name, alpn, false, &mut out);
let st = tls13c_state(c);
let chosen = tls13c_alpn(c);
let none = blen(chosen) == 0;
bfree(chosen);
tls13c_free(c);
vec_free(out);
bfree(alpn);
bfree(name);
bfree(k);
bfree(s);
bfree(r);
if st != 0 || !none { return 1; }
```

### `tls13c_new_opts`

```bastio
fn tls13c_new_opts(random: &Bytes, session_id: &Bytes, priv_key: &Bytes, name: &Bytes, alpn: &Bytes, opts: u64, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> Tls13Client
  requires blen(random) == 32 && blen(session_id) == 32 && blen(priv_key) == 32 && blen(name) <= 255 && blen(alpn) <= 256
  ensures tls13c_ok(result) && result.state == 0
  ensures vlen(out) > vlen(old(out))
```

`tls13c_new_with` with options as bits: 8 offers TLS 1.2 only (a server
that answers with TLS 1.3 fails the connection), 1 accepts a chain the roots do not
vouch for (`verify` false), 2 offers TLS 1.2 as well (for servers and
proxies that do not speak TLS 1.3: ECDHE with X25519, AES-GCM or
ChaCha20-Poly1305, the extended master secret when the server has it, no
renegotiation; a TLS 1.3 server that is made to fall back is noticed by
the value RFC 8446 puts at the end of its random).

Example:

```bastio
let r = balloc(32);
let s = balloc(32);
let k = balloc(32);
let name = bfrom("example.com");
let alpn = balloc(0);
let mut out = text_new();
let c = tls13c_new_opts(r, s, k, name, alpn, 2, &mut out);
let st = tls13c_state(c);
let v = tls13c_version(c);
tls13c_free(c);
vec_free(out);
bfree(alpn);
bfree(name);
bfree(k);
bfree(s);
bfree(r);
if st != 0 || v != 772 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13c_blank`

```bastio
fn tls13c_blank() -> Tls13Client
  ensures result.state == 7
```

A client that has already failed (state 7) and holds no keys or secrets:
a placeholder for a slot whose connection is gone. Callers use it instead
of building the struct, so new fields do not break them.

Example:

```bastio
let c = tls13c_blank();
let st = tls13c_state(c);
tls13c_free(c);
if st != 7 { return 1; }
```

```bastio
fn tls13c_free(c: Tls13Client)
```

Frees a client.

### `tls13c_version`

```bastio
fn tls13c_version(c: &Tls13Client) -> u64
```

The protocol version in use: 772 (TLS 1.3), or 771 once a server chose
TLS 1.2.

Example:

```bastio
let c = tls13c_blank();
let v = tls13c_version(c);
tls13c_free(c);
if v != 772 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13c_suite`

```bastio
fn tls13c_suite(c: &Tls13Client) -> u64
```

The cipher suite in use (its IANA number, 0x1301.. for TLS 1.3 or
0xC02B.. for TLS 1.2); 0 before the ServerHello.

Example:

```bastio
let c = tls13c_blank();
let s = tls13c_suite(c);
tls13c_free(c);
if s != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13c_check`

```bastio
fn tls13c_check(c: &Tls13Client) -> bool
  ensures result ==> tls13c_ok(c)
```

Whether `c` has the sizes and states the other functions require
(`tls13c_ok`): true for a client made by `tls13c_new` or
`tls13c_new_with` and kept by these functions, false for a blank one.
Callers that keep clients in a vector use it after taking one out.

Example:

```bastio
let c = tls13c_blank();
let ok = tls13c_check(c);
tls13c_free(c);
if ok { return 1; }
```

### `tls13c_alpn`

```bastio
fn tls13c_alpn(c: &Tls13Client) -> Bytes
```

The application protocol the server chose (a copy; empty when it chose
none or has not answered yet).

Example:

```bastio
let c = tls13c_blank();
let a = tls13c_alpn(c);
let n = blen(a);
bfree(a);
tls13c_free(c);
if n != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13c_verdict`

```bastio
fn tls13c_verdict(c: &Tls13Client) -> u64
```

0 when the server's certificate chain was checked and good; otherwise 10
when only the host name is not the certificate's, or 6 (the code a client
that verifies fails with in both cases; a client that verifies keeps the
refused certificate and this verdict too, after the failure).

Example:

```bastio
let c = tls13c_blank();
let v = tls13c_verdict(c);
tls13c_free(c);
if v != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13c_peer_cert`

```bastio
fn tls13c_peer_cert(c: &Tls13Client) -> Bytes
```

The server's own certificate (DER, a copy), once the client has it
(state 3 or later); empty before.

Example:

```bastio
let c = tls13c_blank();
let p = tls13c_peer_cert(c);
let n = blen(p);
bfree(p);
tls13c_free(c);

```

### `tls13c_state`

```bastio
fn tls13c_state(c: &Tls13Client) -> u64
```

The state of `c`: 0 waiting for the ServerHello, 1 for the
EncryptedExtensions, 2 for the Certificate, 3 for the CertificateVerify, 4
for the Finished, 5 connected, 6 closed by the peer, 7 failed. A server
still waiting for the client's certificate is in state 4 too.

### `tls13c_identity`

```bastio
fn tls13c_identity(c: &mut Tls13Client, chain: &Bytes, kind: u64, ka: &Bytes, kb: &Bytes, nonce: &Bytes)
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(chain) < 1048576 && blen(ka) < 65536 && blen(kb) < 65536 && blen(nonce) < 1024
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Gives the client a certificate to show if the server asks for one (TLS
1.3): `chain` is the DER certificates, the client's own first, `kind` 1 for
an RSA key (`ka` the modulus, `kb` the private exponent, signing with
rsa_pss_rsae_sha256) or 2 for an ECDSA P-256 key (`ka` the scalar), and
`nonce` 32 unpredictable bytes. A server that asks and a client without a
usable key get an empty Certificate.

Example:

```bastio
let mut c = tls13c_blank();
let chain = balloc(0);
let ka = balloc(32);
let kb = balloc(0);
let nonce = balloc(32);
if tls13c_check(c) { tls13c_identity(&mut c, chain, 2, ka, kb, nonce); }
bfree(nonce);
bfree(kb);
bfree(ka);
bfree(chain);
tls13c_free(c);
```

### `tls13c_feed`

```bastio
fn tls13c_feed(c: &mut Tls13Client, data: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes, now: u64, out: &mut Vec[u8], app: &mut Vec[u8]) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(data) < 1048576 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Gives the client the bytes `data` that arrived from the server. Whole
records are handled in turn; what they ask the client to send is appended
to `out`, application data from the server to `app`. `roots` are the
trusted certificates (DER, one after the other) and `now` the time in
seconds since 1970. Returns 0, or an error code once the connection has
failed (and `tls13c_state` is 7): 1 malformed, 2 unexpected message, 3 bad
ServerHello, 4 bad key exchange, 5 decryption failed, 6 certificate
rejected, 7 bad signature, 8 bad Finished, 9 alert from the server.

Example:

```bastio
let r = balloc(32);
let s = balloc(32);
let k = balloc(32);
let name = bfrom("example.com");
let mut out = text_new();
let mut app = text_new();
let mut c = tls13c_new(r, s, k, name, &mut out);
let junk = balloc(8);
let roots = balloc(0);
let code = tls13c_feed(&mut c, junk, roots, 1800000000, &mut out, &mut app);
let st = tls13c_state(c);
tls13c_free(c);
vec_free(app);
vec_free(out);
bfree(roots);
bfree(junk);
bfree(name);
bfree(k);
bfree(s);
bfree(r);
if code == 0 || st != 7 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13c_send`

```bastio
fn tls13c_send(c: &mut Tls13Client, data: &Bytes, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> bool
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(data) < 1073741824
```

Seals `data` as application data records and appends them to `out`. False
unless the handshake is complete.

Example:

```bastio
let r = balloc(32);
let s = balloc(32);
let k = balloc(32);
let name = bfrom("example.com");
let mut out = text_new();
let mut c = tls13c_new(r, s, k, name, &mut out);
let data = bfrom("hello");
let sent = tls13c_send(&mut c, data, &mut out);
tls13c_free(c);
vec_free(out);
bfree(data);
bfree(name);
bfree(k);
bfree(s);
bfree(r);
if sent { return 1; }
```

### `tls13c_close`

```bastio
fn tls13c_close(c: &mut Tls13Client, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> bool
  requires tls13c_ok(c)
```

Appends a close_notify alert to `out` and closes the connection on this
side. False unless the handshake is complete.

Example:

```bastio
let r = balloc(32);
let s = balloc(32);
let k = balloc(32);
let name = bfrom("example.com");
let mut out = text_new();
let mut c = tls13c_new(r, s, k, name, &mut out);
let closed = tls13c_close(&mut c, &mut out);
tls13c_free(c);
vec_free(out);
bfree(name);
bfree(k);
bfree(s);
bfree(r);
if closed { return 1; }
```

### `tls13c_shutdown`

```bastio
fn tls13c_shutdown(c: &mut Tls13Client, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> bool
  requires tls13c_ok(c)
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Appends a close_notify alert to `out` and closes the sending side only:
`tls13c_send` refuses from now on, but `tls13c_feed` still takes what the
server sends until it closes too (state 6). False unless the handshake is
complete (or it was already shut).

Example:

```bastio
let r = balloc(32);
let s = balloc(32);
let k = balloc(32);
let name = bfrom("example.com");
let mut out = text_new();
let mut c = tls13c_new(r, s, k, name, &mut out);
let shut = tls13c_shutdown(&mut c, &mut out);
tls13c_free(c);
vec_free(out);
bfree(name);
bfree(k);
bfree(s);
bfree(r);
if shut { return 1; }
```

## Specification functions

### `tls13c_secrets`

```bastio
spec fn tls13c_secrets(c: &Tls13Client, n: u64) -> bool {
  blen(c.hs_secret) == n && blen(c.c_hs) == n && blen(c.s_hs) == n && blen(c.c_secret) == n && blen(c.s_secret) == n
}
```

Internal: the handshake and traffic secrets of `c` all have `n` bytes, the
output length of the hash of the cipher suite (32 for SHA-256, 48 for
SHA-384).

### `tls13c_ok`

```bastio
spec fn tls13c_ok(c: &Tls13Client) -> bool {
  c.state <= 9 && blen(c.priv_key) == 32
    && ((c.suite == 4866 && tls13c_secrets(c, 48)) || ((c.suite == 4865 || c.suite == 4867) && tls13c_secrets(c, 32)))
    && ((c.c_suite == 4867 && blen(c.c_key) == 32) || (c.c_suite == 4866 && blen(c.c_key) == 32) || (c.c_suite == 4865 && blen(c.c_key) == 16))
    && ((c.s_suite == 4867 && blen(c.s_key) == 32) || (c.s_suite == 4866 && blen(c.s_key) == 32) || (c.s_suite == 4865 && blen(c.s_key) == 16))
    && blen(c.c_iv) == 12 && blen(c.s_iv) == 12
    && blen(c.name) <= 255
    && blen(c.transcript) < 1073741824 && blen(c.inbuf) < 1073741824 && blen(c.hsbuf) < 1073741824 && blen(c.leaf) < 1048576
    && blen(c.alpn) <= 256 && blen(c.rnd) <= 64 && blen(c.ms) <= 48
    && blen(c.sk_a) < 65536 && blen(c.sk_b) < 65536
    && blen(c.croots) < 274877906944 && blen(c.cleaf) < 1048576 && blen(c.ck_nonce) < 1024
}
```

Internal: the sizes of the keys and secrets the record layer needs.

## Internals

### `tls13c_base`

```bastio
fn tls13c_base() -> Bytes
  ensures blen(result) == 32
```

Internal: the 9 as a field element, the base point of X25519.

### `tls13c_plain_record`

```bastio
fn tls13c_plain_record(t: &mut Vec[u8], ty: u8, body: &Bytes)
  requires blen(body) <= 16384
  ensures vlen(t) == vlen(old(t)) + 5 + blen(body)
```

Internal: the record of type `ty` (with the legacy version 0x0303, or
0x0301 for `legacy` = 1) around `body`.

### `tls13c_fail`

```bastio
fn tls13c_fail(c: &mut Tls13Client, code: u64) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && code >= 1
  ensures tls13c_ok(c) && result == code && c.state == 7
```

Internal: marks `c` failed and returns `code`.

### `tls13c_append`

```bastio
fn tls13c_append(buf: Bytes, more: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(buf) < 1073741824 && blen(more) < 1073741824
  ensures blen(result) == blen(buf) + blen(more)
```

Internal: replaces `buf` with `buf` followed by `more`.

### `tls13c_hash`

```bastio
fn tls13c_hash(c: &Tls13Client) -> Bytes
  requires tls13c_ok(c)
  ensures blen(result) == blen(c.hs_secret)
```

Internal: the hash of the handshake messages so far.

### `tls13c_note`

```bastio
fn tls13c_note(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes) -> bool
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: adds the handshake message `msg` to the transcript.

### `tls13c_u24`

```bastio
fn tls13c_u24(b: &Bytes, at: u64) -> u64
  requires at + 3 <= blen(b)
  ensures result < 16777216
```

Internal: the 24-bit number at `b[at..at+3]`.

### `tls13c_u16`

```bastio
fn tls13c_u16(b: &Bytes, at: u64) -> u64
  requires at + 2 <= blen(b)
  ensures result < 65536
```

Internal: the 16-bit number at `b[at..at+2]`.

### `tls13c_link`

```bastio
fn tls13c_link(msg: &Bytes, inner: Span, outer: Span, now: u64) -> bool
  requires inner.start <= inner.end && inner.end <= blen(msg) && outer.start <= outer.end && outer.end <= blen(msg) && blen(msg) < 274877906944
```

Internal: whether the certificate of `inner` (a span of `msg`) was signed
by the one of `outer`, both are valid at `now` and `outer` may sign.

### `tls13c_anchored`

```bastio
fn tls13c_anchored(msg: &Bytes, last: Span, roots: &Bytes, now: u64) -> bool
  requires last.start <= last.end && last.end <= blen(msg) && blen(msg) < 274877906944 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
```

Internal: whether the last certificate of the chain (the span `last` of
`msg`) is one of the trusted `roots` (certificates one after the other) or
was signed by one that may sign and is valid at `now`.

### `tls13c_chain`

```bastio
fn tls13c_chain(msg: &Bytes, name: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes, now: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(msg) < 1048576 && blen(name) <= 255 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) < 1048576
```

Internal: checks the Certificate message `msg` (with its header) for a
server named `name` at time `now` against `roots`, and returns the
server's own certificate if it is good.

### `tls13c_chain_for`

```bastio
fn tls13c_chain_for(msg: &Bytes, name: &Bytes, check_name: bool, roots: &Bytes, now: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(msg) < 1048576 && blen(name) <= 255 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) < 1048576
```

Internal: `tls13c_chain`, with the check of the host name only when
`check_name`.

### `tls13c_first_cert`

```bastio
fn tls13c_first_cert(msg: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) < 1048576
```

Internal: the first certificate of the Certificate message `msg` (the
server's own), if it is one x509_parse reads.

### `tls13c_all_zero`

```bastio
fn tls13c_all_zero(b: &Bytes) -> bool
```

Internal: 1 if all of `b` is zero.

### `tls13c_keys`

```bastio
fn tls13c_keys(c: &mut Tls13Client, secret: &Bytes, write: bool)
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(secret) == blen(c.hs_secret)
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: installs the traffic keys for the client's writing (`write`) or
reading side from the `secret` (as long as the hash of the suite).

### `tls13c_set_suite`

```bastio
fn tls13c_set_suite(c: &mut Tls13Client, suite: u64)
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && (suite == 4865 || suite == 4866 || suite == 4867)
  ensures tls13c_ok(c) && c.suite == suite
```

Internal: switches `c` to the cipher suite `suite`, which fixes the hash
and so the length of the secrets: they are replaced by zeros of the right
length (they are made anew from the key exchange right after).

### `tls13c_handshake_keys`

```bastio
fn tls13c_handshake_keys(c: &mut Tls13Client, share: &Bytes) -> bool
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(share) == 32
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: the handshake secrets from the server's key share `share`
(32 bytes), with the ServerHello already in the transcript.

### `tls13c_application_keys`

```bastio
fn tls13c_application_keys(c: &mut Tls13Client)
  requires tls13c_ok(c)
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: the application traffic secrets and keys, with the server's
Finished already in the transcript.

### `tls13c_application_keys_for`

```bastio
fn tls13c_application_keys_for(c: &mut Tls13Client, h: &Bytes)
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(h) == blen(c.hs_secret)
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: the application keys for the transcript hash `h` (through the
server's Finished).

### `tls13c_server_hello`

```bastio
fn tls13c_server_hello(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: handles a ServerHello `msg` (state 0).

### `tls13c_offered`

```bastio
fn tls13c_offered(list: &Bytes, name: &Bytes) -> bool
```

Internal: whether `name` is one of the names of the ProtocolNameList
contents `list` (each behind a one-byte length).

### `tls13c_encrypted_extensions`

```bastio
fn tls13c_encrypted_extensions(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: handles EncryptedExtensions `msg` (state 1): the extensions are
read for their lengths and not used.

### `tls13c_certificate`

```bastio
fn tls13c_certificate(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes, now: u64) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: handles the Certificate `msg` (state 2).

### `tls13c_signed_content`

```bastio
fn tls13c_signed_content(h: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(h) == 32 || blen(h) == 48
  ensures blen(result) == 98 + blen(h)
```

Internal: what the server signs in its CertificateVerify (RFC 8446
section 4.4.3): 64 spaces, a label, a zero byte and the transcript hash.

### `tls13c_certificate_verify`

```bastio
fn tls13c_certificate_verify(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: handles the CertificateVerify `msg` (state 3).

### `tls13c_send_record`

```bastio
fn tls13c_send_record(c: &mut Tls13Client, ty: u8, plain: &Bytes, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> bool
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(plain) <= 16384
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: appends a record of type `ty` carrying `plain`, sealed with
the client's keys, to `out`.

### `tls13c_send_message`

```bastio
fn tls13c_send_message(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> bool
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: adds the handshake message `msg` to the transcript and sends it,
sealed with the client's keys, in as many records as it takes.

### `tls13c_client_flight`

```bastio
fn tls13c_client_flight(c: &mut Tls13Client, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c)
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: sends the client's Certificate, and its CertificateVerify when
the server asked for a certificate and the client has one that fits.

### `tls13c_finished`

```bastio
fn tls13c_finished(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: handles the server's Finished `msg` (state 4), sends the
client's, and switches to the application keys.

### `tls13c_update_secret`

```bastio
fn tls13c_update_secret(secret: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(secret) == 32 || blen(secret) == 48
  ensures blen(result) == blen(secret)
```

Internal: the next traffic secret after `secret` (RFC 8446 section 7.2).

### `tls13c_after`

```bastio
fn tls13c_after(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: handles a handshake message `msg` after the handshake (state 5):
NewSessionTicket is ignored and KeyUpdate changes the keys.

### `tls13c_cert_request`

```bastio
fn tls13c_cert_request(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: handles a CertificateRequest `msg` (state 2): the client picks
a signature scheme for its own key, or none.

### `tls13c_message`

```bastio
fn tls13c_message(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes, now: u64, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: handles the handshake message `msg` for the state of `c`.

### `tls13c_handshake_data`

```bastio
fn tls13c_handshake_data(c: &mut Tls13Client, plain: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes, now: u64, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(plain) <= 16640 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: handles the handshake bytes `plain` that arrived in a record:
they are joined to what is left of earlier ones and cut into messages.

### `tls13c_record`

```bastio
fn tls13c_record(c: &mut Tls13Client, rec: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes, now: u64, out: &mut Vec[u8], app: &mut Vec[u8]) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(rec) >= 5 && blen(rec) <= 16645 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: handles one whole record `rec` (with its header).

### `tls12c_hmac`

```bastio
fn tls12c_hmac(big: bool, key: &Bytes, msg: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  ensures blen(result) == 32 || blen(result) == 48
```

Internal: an HMAC with SHA-384 when `big`, else with SHA-256.

### `tls12c_prf`

```bastio
fn tls12c_prf(big: bool, secret: &Bytes, label: Str, seed: &Bytes, n: u64) -> Bytes
  requires n <= 256 && slen(label) <= 64 && blen(seed) <= 1024
  ensures blen(result) == n
```

Internal: the TLS 1.2 PRF (P_SHA256, or P_SHA384 when `big`): `n` bytes
from `secret`, the `label` and `seed`.

### `tls12c_aad`

```bastio
fn tls12c_aad(seq: u64, ty: u8, len: u64) -> Bytes
  requires len < 65536
  ensures blen(result) == 13
```

Internal: the additional data of a TLS 1.2 AEAD record: the sequence
number, the type, the version and the length of the plaintext.

### `tls12c_plain`

```bastio
fn tls12c_plain(out: &mut Vec[u8], ty: u8, body: &Bytes)
  requires blen(body) < 65536
```

Internal: appends a TLS 1.2 record of type `ty` with `body` as it is.

### `tls12c_seal`

```bastio
fn tls12c_seal(c: &mut Tls13Client, ty: u8, plain: &Bytes, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> bool
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(plain) <= 16384
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: seals `plain` as a TLS 1.2 record of type `ty` with the
client's keys (AES-GCM with the sequence number as the explicit nonce, or
ChaCha20-Poly1305 with the nonce of RFC 7905) and appends it to `out`.

### `tls12c_open`

```bastio
fn tls12c_open(c: &mut Tls13Client, rec: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(rec) >= 5 && blen(rec) <= 16645
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) <= 16640
```

Internal: opens the TLS 1.2 record `rec` (with its header) with the
server's keys; the plaintext, or None if it is not genuine.

### `tls12c_signed`

```bastio
fn tls12c_signed(leaf: &Bytes, scheme: u64, content: &Bytes, sig: &Bytes) -> bool
  requires blen(content) < 1048576 && blen(sig) < 65536 && blen(leaf) < 1048576
```

Internal: does the signature `sig` with the scheme `scheme` (a TLS
SignatureScheme) over `content` check out with the key of the
certificate `leaf`?

### `tls12c_server_hello`

```bastio
fn tls12c_server_hello(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: the ServerHello `msg` if it is one for TLS 1.2 (no
supported_versions extension); returns 1000 when it is not, for the TLS
1.3 path to take it.

### `tls12c_certificate`

```bastio
fn tls12c_certificate(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes, now: u64) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: the TLS 1.2 Certificate `msg`, checked as `tls13c_certificate`
checks a TLS 1.3 one (it is rewritten in that form first).

### `tls12c_key_exchange`

```bastio
fn tls12c_key_exchange(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: the ServerKeyExchange `msg`: an X25519 share signed with the
key of the server's certificate over both randoms and the parameters.

### `tls12c_keys`

```bastio
fn tls12c_keys(c: &mut Tls13Client)
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(c.rnd) == 64 && blen(c.ms) == 48
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: the key block from the master secret: the write keys and IVs
(an AES-GCM salt of 4 bytes is kept as the first 4 of 12, then zeros, so
tls13_nonce puts the sequence number behind it).

### `tls12c_hello_done`

```bastio
fn tls12c_hello_done(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: the ServerHelloDone `msg`: the client sends its share, changes
to the new keys and sends its Finished.

### `tls12c_finished`

```bastio
fn tls12c_finished(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: the server's Finished `msg` (after its ChangeCipherSpec).

### `tls12c_message`

```bastio
fn tls12c_message(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes, now: u64, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: a handshake message for a client that offered TLS 1.2 (the
ServerHello, then the TLS 1.2 flight when the server chose it).

### `tls12c_handshake_data`

```bastio
fn tls12c_handshake_data(c: &mut Tls13Client, plain: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes, now: u64, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(plain) <= 16640 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: handshake bytes for `tls12c_message`, cut into messages.

### `tls12c_record`

```bastio
fn tls12c_record(c: &mut Tls13Client, rec: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes, now: u64, out: &mut Vec[u8], app: &mut Vec[u8]) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(rec) >= 5 && blen(rec) <= 16645 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: one whole record `rec` for a client that is in TLS 1.2.
